QF.id: SIA Logic Model for Social Programs_14

question.text: Under the Logic Model, 'Inputs' are categorised into:

answer.text: Financial resources (monetary) and non-financial resources (human, community, organisational, intellectual, and other non-monetary resources)

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 4.3(v), Inputs are resources invested or deployed to achieve intended results. They are categorised into Financial resources (monetary aspects) and Non-financial resources (human, community, organisational, intellectual and other non-monetary resources). This twin categorisation matters because SROI and impact cost computations often under-value non-cash inputs. The Trap: A ignores non-cash inputs — a common valuation mistake. C omits financial inputs. B is overly narrow. Cross-Exam Context: Cross-relevant to SAS-200/400 assurance engagements (XXIII Ch 7) and to SROI/valuation exercises picked up in X-A Investment Adviser and XV Research Analyst modules. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Ask the SE to value in-kind inputs (volunteer hours, donated premises, pro-bono services) at market rates in a separate schedule. Under-valued inputs inflate SROI ratios and mislead donors.
